title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Senior Data Engineer

This role is a Hybrid work model

Location: Mumbai (Jogeshwari)

Shift: 12 pm - 8 pm (IST)


Come work on fantastically high-scale systems with us! Blis is an award-winning, global leader and technology innovator in big data analytics and advertising. We help brands such as McDonald's, Samsung, and Mercedes-Benz to understand and effectively reach their best audiences


In doing this, we are industry champions in our commitment to the ethical use of data and believe people should have control over their data and privacy. With offices across four continents, we are a truly international company with a global culture and scale.

We are looking for solid and experienced Data Engineers to work on building out secure, automated, scalable pipelines on GCP. We receive over 350gb of data an hour and respond to 400,000 decision requests each second, with petabytes of analytical data to work with.We tackle challenges across almost every major discipline of data science, including classification, clustering, optimisation, and data mining. You will be responsible for building stable production level pipelines, maximising the efficiency of cloud compute to ensure that data is properly enabled for operational and scientific causes.


As of March 2025, Blis was acquired by T-Mobile and is now part of T-Mobile Advertising Solutions. This is a growing team with big responsibilities and exciting challenges ahead of it, as we look to reach the next 10x level of scale and intelligence.


At Blis, Data Engineers are a combination of software engineers, cloud engineers, and data processing engineers. They actively design and build production pipeline code, typically in Python, whilst having practical experience in ensuring, policing, and measuring for good data governance, quality, and efficient consumption. To run an efficient landscape we are ideally looking for candidates that are comfortable with event- driven automation across also aspects of our operational pipelines.


As a Blis data engineer, we seek to understand the data and problem definition and find efficient solutions, so critical thinking is a key component to efficient pipelines and effective reuse, this must include defining the pipelines for the correct controls and recovery points not only function and scale. Across the team, everyone supports each other through mentoring, brainstorming, and pairing up. They have a passion for delivering products that delight and astound our customers and that have a long-lasting impact on the business. They do this while also optimising themselves and the team for long-lasting agility, which is often synonymous with practicing Good Engineering. They are almost always adherents of Lean Development and work well in environments with significant amounts of freedom and ambitious goals


Key responsibilities

  • Design, build, monitor, and support large scale data processing pipelines.
  • Support, mentor, and pair with other members of the team to advance our team’s capabilities and capacity.
  • Help Blis explore and exploit new data streams to innovative and support commercial and technical growth
  • Work closely with Product and be comfortable with taking, making and delivering against fast paced decisions to delight our customers. This ideal candidate will be comfortable with fast feature delivery with a robust engineered follow up.


Skills and requirements

  • 8+ years direct experience delivering robust performant data pipelines within the constraints of direct SLA’s and commercial financial footprints.
  • Proven experience in architecting, developing, and maintaining Apache Druid and Imply platforms, with a focus on DevOps practices and large-scale system re-architecture
  • Mastery of building Pipelines in GCP maximising the use of native and native supporting technologies e.g. Apache Airflow
  • Mastery of Python for data and computational tasks with fluency in data cleansing, validation and composition techniques.
  • Hands-on implementation and architectural familiarity with all forms of data sourcing i.e streaming data, relational and non-relational databases, and distributed processing technologies (e.g. Spark)Fluency with all appropriate python libraries typical of data science e.g. pandas, scikit-learn, scipy, numpy, MLlib and/or other machine learning and statistical libraries
  • Advanced knowledge of cloud based services specifically GCPExcellent working understanding of server-side LinuxProfessional in managing and updating on tasks ensuring appropriate levels of documentation, testing and assurance around their solution
  • Desired Experience optimizing both code and config in Spark, Hive, or similar toolsPractical experience working with relational databases, including advanced operations such as partitioning and indexing


Knowledge and experience with tools like AWS Athena or Google BigQuery to solve data-centric problems Understanding and ability to innovate, apply, and optimize complex algorithms and statistical techniques to large data structuresExperience with Python Notebooks, such as Jupyter, Zeppelin, or Google Datalabto analyze, prototype, and visualize data and algorithmic output


About us

Blis is the only omnichannel DSP that unites telco data, real-world movement patterns, and transactions to deliver a complete view of the consumer. Powered by T-Mobile and built for precision at scale, Blis' omnichannel platform helps marketers map the full purchase journey – from impression to transaction – and expand their audience reach, driving incremental results across every screen.

title: Head of Manufacturing Engineering
description:
Mission

TAR’s mission is to power intelligence for the world. We are building the world’s first off-grid power plant for data centers powered by renewable technologies.

We firmly believe AI should be built in the US for the benefit of all people. For that, power must be fast, clean and scalable. We are singularly focused on delivering GW-scale power faster than anyone has ever done, by rethinking every layer of the stack.

We vertically integrate to solve every bottleneck, from racking systems to power electronics to dispatch algorithms to on-site construction.

Leave your mark on the future of civilization-scale energy infrastructure.

Company

TAR is both a hardware and software company, we are building out massive, critical, physical infrastructure. TAR is working directly with one of the largest compute providers to scale and deploy 5GWs by 2028.

We operate on…

  • High ownership. High Agency. Own project end-to-end. Great people don’t need to be managed.

  • Speed. We achieve great things on incredible timelines. We push ourselves to go faster.

  • First principles. No ego. No hierarchy. Challenge every assumption.

  • Passion. Solving the energy problem is one of the largest challenges that faces the world now and in the future.

About the role

TAR builds its own construction robots to install its proprietary racking at gigawatt scale, and building those machines at rate is its own engineering discipline. As the fleet grows from prototypes to production across multiple robot programs, manufacturing engineering becomes the constraint on how fast TAR can put working machines in the field. As Head of Manufacturing Engineering, you own that discipline company-wide. You take TAR from single-line, hands-on builds to a manufacturing engineering organization with the standards, quality systems, and capital and capacity planning to scale from low-rate production to reliable, higher-volume manufacturing across every program. This is a senior leadership seat, based at our San Francisco robotics facility.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own the manufacturing engineering strategy and roadmap across TAR's robotics product lines, aligning capacity, tooling, and process investment with the company's scaling plans.

  • Build and lead the manufacturing engineering organization, hiring, structuring, and developing engineers and engineering leads as the function grows beyond a single line.

  • Own capital equipment and capacity planning, forecasting the headcount, tooling, and facility investment needed to scale from prototype and low-rate production to reliable, higher-volume manufacturing across multiple programs.

  • Set the manufacturing engineering standards, quality systems, and documentation practices that apply company-wide, so every product line meets the same bar for austere-environment reliability instead of reinventing process line by line.

  • Own supplier and contract manufacturer strategy at the organizational level, setting the criteria by which manufacturing partners are selected, negotiated with, and held accountable.

  • Establish company-wide root-cause and continuous-improvement processes so lessons from any single line or product feed back into how every future line is built.

  • Serve as the senior manufacturing engineering voice on the leadership team, shaping investment decisions, make-versus-buy trade-offs, and production timelines with engineering, supply chain, and executive leadership.

  • Represent manufacturing engineering externally with customers, partners, and investors when technical and operational credibility earns trust.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of manufacturing engineering experience, including 5+ years in a leadership role (Director, Head of, or VP level) building and running a manufacturing engineering organization, not a single line.

  • Demonstrated experience scaling manufacturing engineering across multiple product lines, programs, or sites, beyond standing up one assembly line.

  • Track record owning capital equipment planning and budget for manufacturing scale-up, including make-versus-buy and contract manufacturer decisions at a strategic level.

  • Experience building and leading a team of manufacturing engineers and engineering leads, including hiring and developing people managers.

  • Deep expertise across the manufacturing value chain: DFM, tooling, process development, and quality systems, with the ability to set standards other engineers execute against.

  • Strong communication skills, comfortable representing manufacturing engineering decisions to executive leadership, customers, and investors.

Nice to have

  • Experience manufacturing hardware for austere, field, or defense-adjacent environments.

  • Experience scaling manufacturing engineering at a high-growth, venture-backed hardware or robotics company, such as Anduril, SpaceX, or Tesla.

  • Familiarity with formal quality systems (ISO, AS9100) applied at an organizational rather than single-line level.

  • Experience standing up a manufacturing engineering function from its first hire, including building out the managers and leads beneath you.

Salary and Benefits

  • Up to $15K relocation bonus

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

  • $1K monthly stipend for meals

title: Lead
description:
Gosincro, also known as Sincro, is a part of the Easyship Group portfolio of companies, and our shipping platform connects sellers and marketplaces to buyers around the world shipping over 30 million parcels from 30+ origin countries to almost 200 destination countries in 2023. We are a diverse group, consisting of more than 20 nationalities based across our London, Chicago, Los Angeles, Toronto, Singapore, and Hong Kong offices. Sincro is a part of a global network of facilities specializing in ecommerce and the logistics market.


Job Summary:

title: Senior Software Engineer (AI Inference & Runtime Platform)
description:
About AZX

Our mission is to accelerate positive impact in critical industries through AI transformation. We specialize in physics-informed ML and enterprise AI solutions that directly address climate and sustainability challenges.

We’re growing quickly and already work with category-leaders in real estate (CBRE), energy (LevelTen Energy), logistics (Flexe) and utilities.

We’re a public benefit corporation, founded in 2024, and have been profitable from inception.

We work on challenges in clean energy, decarbonization, climate risk, energy systems, and global economics. We’re building our company for long-term success and aim to create the ultimate place to work for those passionate about AI and making a positive impact.

About This Role:

You will be responsible for owning the layer where AI work physically happens: the machines, the isolation boundary, and the models running on them. This role anchors on two systems. The first is our inference control plane — open-weight models and custom task-model zoos, hosted and operated across managed GPU clouds and customer-managed Kubernetes clusters, with scale-to-zero economics, cold-start discipline, and per-token cost accounting that stays correct even when a client disconnects mid-stream — along with the Kubernetes layer those workloads live on: operators, autoscaling, node lifecycle. The second is our agent-sandboxing platform: hardware-isolated microVMs for running untrusted, agent-generated code securely and compliantly by construction, where agents operate with least privilege, never see a credential, and a human gates anything that writes to a system of record. You'll write Rust in the morning, a Kubernetes controller after lunch, and a FastAPI control-plane endpoint before you go home — building the fork engine, the guest agent, and the multi-substrate model lifecycle. We're looking for individuals who've built this class of stack (an inference-serving or serverless-GPU platform), operated it hard at scale, or ideally both.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage the serving tier for open-weight models: engine deployment and configuration, cold-start strategy, per-model SLOs, and upgrade/canary discipline.

  • Administer the Kubernetes layer for inference and sandbox workloads: operators and CRDs, autoscaling (KEDA/Karpenter-class), GPU scheduling and sharing, and node lifecycle.

  • Own the stateful data plane: hosted vector stores for semantic memory and graph stores for knowledge graphs — deployed, backed up, scaled, and recovered, with restores that are tested rather than hoped for.

  • Oversee the sandbox runtime and its host-side control plane: lifecycle, exec, snapshot/fork, teardown, metering, and the threat model of the isolation boundary.

  • Direct the FastAPI control-plane services, Terraform/OpenTofu, Bicep, and the dashboards

  • Run the layer the backend services team builds on, expect to debug into their services, and expect them to read your dashboards.

  • Manage the open-source posture: build to OSS standards and release as it matures, with reviewed PRs, real docs, and reproducible builds.

Core Qualifications

  • 5+ years of shipping production systems in a systems language. Rust is the house language, but polyglots are welcome — deep Go, C/C++, or Zig with genuine appetite for Rust counts. Async runtimes, memory-safety discipline, and debugging at the syscall boundary should be familiar territory.

  • Operated Kubernetes workloads that other people depended on — controllers or operators, scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle. You've been paged, and the experience changed how you build.

  • Strong ability to threat-model isolation boundaries (namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, hypervisors), including identifying what an untrusted guest could observe, forge, or exhaust, and applying security best practices for agentic execution — least privilege, no credentials in the sandbox, audit trails, and human approval on write actions.

  • Hands-on experience deploying or operating open-weight LLM serving infrastructure (vLLM/SGLang or similar), including packaging models into reliable, metered production endpoints.

  • Performance discipline in distributed systems: you measure before you optimize, and you can tell the story of a latency you killed with the numbers attached.

  • Practical depth in some of our core stack — Rust (tokio), Python/FastAPI, Kubernetes operators (controller-runtime/Kubebuilder/CRDs), KEDA, Karpenter, GPU device plugins/DRA — with a genuine willingness to research your way into the rest.

  • Familiarity with isolation technology (Firecracker, Kata, gVisor, or comparable), secrets management and egress control (Vault/KMS-class), and hosting stateful systems (vector stores like pgvector/Qdrant, graph stores like Neo4j) with backup and failover discipline.

  • Comfort operating across cloud and GPU substrates — AWS/Azure/GCP plus managed GPU clouds — using infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/OpenTofu, Bicep) and observability tooling (OpenTelemetry).

  • Bachelor's Degree; Master's is a plus

Why AZX!

  • Be part of a fast-growing, profitable, mission-driven company with industry-leading clients tackling the massive opportunity of AI transformation in critical industries.

  • Competitive early-stage startup compensation (based on capabilities, experience, and location)

  • Bonus eligibility

  • Health insurance with meaningful coverage for dependents

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Equity

  • Fully remote culture with a cluster of teammates in Seattle

Additional Information:

  • Must be able to travel 2x/year for company summits

  • Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

  • We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time.

  • Please only apply to a maximum of 2 roles at a time, any applicants who apply to more then 2 roles within a 6 month period will automatically be disqualified

Next Steps:

title: Chief Security Officer
description:
L3Harris is dedicated to recruiting and developing high-performing talent who are passionate about what they do. Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. Fundamental to our culture is an unwavering focus on values, dedication to our communities, and commitment to excellence in everything we do.

L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.


About the role

The Manager, Industrial Security / Chief Security Officer (CSO) is responsible for establishing, maintaining and continually improving L3H GS2A's protective security framework and ensuring compliance with Defence Industry Security Program (DISP) membership obligations.

Acting as the principal advisor to the Managing Director and Senior Leadership Team (SLT) on all security matters, the CSO provides strategic leadership and governance across personnel, physical, information and industrial security domains to ensure L3H GS2A effectively manages security risks while supporting business growth and operational objectives.

The role is accountable for developing security strategies, policies and programs that protect personnel, facilities, information, technologies and commercial interests while ensuring compliance with applicable Australian Government security requirements, including DISP, PSPF, DSPF and ISM obligations.

The CSO will work closely with Defence customers, government agencies, senior leadership and program teams to ensure security considerations are embedded into business planning, project execution, risk management and organisational decision making.


What the role will involve

Key Business Operations Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement and maintain the L3H GS2A Security Management System.

  • Lead security governance activities and provide strategic security advice to the MD and SLT.

  • Ensure compliance with Defence Industry Security Program (DISP) obligations and maintain organisational readiness for Defence assurance activities and audits.

  • Establish and maintain organisational security policies, standards, procedures and work instructions

  • Develop and maintain the Security Risk Management Plan and associated security assurance activities

  • Monitor emerging threats, vulnerabilities and regulatory changes and implement appropriate mitigation actions

  • Manage the organisation's security governance forums and provide regular reporting on security performance, risks and compliance

Key Protective Security Responsibilities

  • Provide oversight of personnel, physical, information and industrial security functions across the organisation

  • Develop and maintain site security plans, risk assessments and security operating procedures

  • Ensure ongoing compliance with Australian Government security requirements including PSPF, DSPF and Information Security Manual (ISM) controls

  • Maintain oversight of security accreditations, certifications and facility security requirements

  • Support secure facility operations and management of classified information environments

  • Coordinate security programs supporting domestic and international business operations where required.

Key Personnel Security Responsibilities

  • Maintain oversight of security clearance sponsorship and personnel security management activities

  • Ensure effective ongoing assessment and management of personnel suitability

  • Manage security awareness, induction and refresher training programs

  • Implement and maintain Insider Threat Program arrangements and supporting policies

  • Promote a strong organisational security culture through education, awareness and leadership engagement

Key Incident and Risk Management Responsibilities

  • Lead investigations into security incidents, breaches and non-compliance events

  • Coordinate incident reporting, corrective actions and lessons learned activities

  • Manage crisis response and security-related emergency management activities

  • Ensure security risks are identified, assessed, monitored and managed through enterprise risk management processes

  • Develop and implement security improvement initiatives that enhance organisational resilience and maturity.

Key Supply Chain Security Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain supply chain security governance processes

  • Assess supplier security risks and ensure appropriate contractual security obligations are implemented

  • Support subcontractor and partner due diligence activities relating to security compliance and risk

  • Collaborate with Commercial, Procurement and Program teams to ensure security requirements are flowed down appropriately through contracts and agreements

Stakeholder Engagement Responsibilities

  • Act as the primary security interface with Defence, government agencies and relevant industry partners

  • Develop strong working relationships across all business functions to ensure security requirements support operational objectives

  • Effectively communicate security risks, requirements and emerging threats to stakeholders at all levels

  • Provide Chief Security Officer support to associated business units, programs or facilities as required.


Key Accountabilities

  • Maintenance of DISP membership and compliance across all applicable security domains

  • Development, implementation and continual improvement of the L3H GS2A Security Management System

  • Achievement of organisational security objectives and performance measures

  • Effective management of security risks and protection of personnel, facilities, information and assets

  • Maintenance of security policies, procedures and assurance activities

  • Delivery of security awareness, training and Insider Threat Program objectives

  • Timely management and reporting of security incidents and corrective actions

  • Successful completion of security audits, assessments and Defence assurance activities

  • Provision of accurate security reporting and advice to the Managing Director and Senior Leadership Team

  • Development and maintenance of a positive and proactive organisational security culture


Essential Requirements

  • Minimum seven (7) years' experience in a senior security leadership, Industrial Security Manager or Chief Security Officer role

  • Demonstrated experience managing security operations within a Defence Industry Security Program (DISP) environment

  • Extensive knowledge of:

Defence Industry Security Program (DISP)

Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF)

Defence Security Principles Framework (DSPF)

Australian Government Information Security Manual (ISM)

Personnel, physical and information security principles

  • Proven experience developing and implementing security governance frameworks, policies and management systems

  • Demonstrated ability to manage security risks within a complex operational environment

  • Experience leading security investigations, incident response and assurance activities

  • Strong ICT and cyber security awareness

  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain an Australian Government Security Vetting Agency (AGSVA) Negative Vetting Level 2 (NV2) Security Clearance.


About L3Harris Australia

L3Harris has provided advanced technology solutions to government and commercial customers across Australia for more than 25 years. L3Harris has facilities in all major cities and employs over 500 people.

L3Harris in Eight Mile Plains is The Centre of Excellence for Electronic Warfare and is home to world-leading design, manufacture and integration expertise and the sustainment of high-reliability electronic warfare components. Our highly skilled workforce design and develop Australia’s sovereign defence capabilities such as the next-generation space, airborne and cyber capabilities for the Australian warfighter.

description:
About Scalar:

Building on a great API is one of the best feelings in software — every interface you want is right there, and it all just works. Building on a bad one is the opposite: out-of-date docs, no SDK in your language, no MCP server. We started Scalar to fix that.

We're a small team (around ten engineers and designers) who wear a lot of hats and obsess over our craft. We think every company deserves Stripe-level docs, SDKs, and MCP servers from day zero — not just the ones with a platform team to build them. Open-source is in our DNA: our whole team contributes to and maintains repositories across the API ecosystem, including the standards everyone relies on, like OpenAPI.

We keep things lean and move without layers of process — engineers pick up problems, talk to each other, and ship. We're looking for owners with high agency: people who see what needs doing and do it. If you do your best work with a lot of autonomy and very little ego, you'll feel at home here.

The role

Right now, sales at Scalar is Marc, our CEO, doing every part of it himself. Sourcing the account, running the first call, going deep on the technical evaluation, answering the security review, negotiating the contract, onboarding the team, and picking up the Slack message when something breaks at 5pm. That's founder-led sales end to end, and it's worked — it's how we got Zoom, Clerk, Warp, and Profound.

It also doesn't scale, which is why this role exists.

You'll be our first Solutions Engineer and one of the first three people on the sales team, joining alongside two SDRs starting at the same time. You'll sit next to Marc in our San Francisco office, learn the motion from the person who built it, and then take the technical half of it off his plate — the demos, the proofs of concept, the migrations, and the first ninety days of every customer who signs.

There is a motion here and it works — but it's Marc's, it lives largely in his head, and it has never had a technical counterpart. The demo environments, the POC scoping, the technical qualification bar, the answers to the objection you'll hear for the fourth time: none of that exists yet. You'll build it, and what you build is what the next five people on this team will use. If you've been waiting for the job where you shape how a company sells rather than execute how it already does, this is that job.

Who we sell to

Our buyers are engineers, and the product is the proof. Zoom's developer documentation runs on Scalar. So does Clerk's — a company whose docs were already a competitive advantage, which makes them exactly the kind of customer with no reason to switch unless the thing is genuinely better. Warp and Profound ship SDKs we generate from their OpenAPI documents, in every language their users ask for.

Those are the rooms you'll be in: platform teams, API teams, and the staff engineer who has strong opinions about their spec and is not going to be charmed. They don't want a deck. They want to see their own API rendered in Scalar Docs, their SDK generated in their language, and MCP servers available so agents can do real work against their API. Your job is to make that happen fast enough that the decision makes itself.

This is a genuinely technical job, not a sales job with a technical veneer. You'll be writing TypeScript against a prospect's OpenAPI document live on a call, and opening a PR against scalar/scalar the next morning to fix whatever made it hard. The same product surface our platform team runs — Docs, SDK generation, and Agent Scalar — is the surface you'll demo, migrate customers onto, and file reproductions against.

What you'll work on

  • Technical wins — live demos and hands-on POCs against a prospect's real API, not a sandbox. Scoping calls, architecture questions, and the security and compliance reviews nobody else wants to answer

  • Docs migrations — getting teams off Redocly, Mintlify, Stoplight, ReadMe, and homegrown docs sites, including the unglamorous part: cleaning up OpenAPI documents that have drifted from reality for three years, and rebuilding their Markdown/MDX and two-way Git sync so nothing breaks in the cut-over

  • SDK generation — showing an engineering team what their spec produces across TypeScript, Python, Go, PHP, Java, and Ruby, explaining why a oneOf or a missing discriminator makes their SDK ugly, and fixing the spec so it doesn't

  • Agent Scalar — standing up secure MCP servers against a prospect's API and demonstrating what an agent can do with a well-described interface, which is still a new enough argument that you'll be making it for the first time in most rooms

  • Building the motion with Marc — turning founder-led selling into something repeatable: qualification criteria, demo environments, POC scoping that doesn't take three weeks, and the answers to the objections we hear more than twice

  • Building, actually building — sample apps, custom themes, integration glue, reproduction cases, and fixes to our own repos. You'll open PRs against Scalar, not just tickets

  • Onboarding and support — owning the first 90 days of a new customer, and being the technical escalation when an SDK generates something wrong or a CI sync breaks at 5pm

  • Product feedback with evidence — you'll see every gap before anyone else does. We expect you to say so loudly, with a reproduction, and sometimes with a patch

  • The function after you — as we grow the team, you'll set the technical bar for who joins it and train the people who follow you into this role

You might be a fit if

  • You've done customer-facing technical work — solutions or sales engineering, forward-deployed, developer relations, or consulting — and you can hold your own with a skeptical staff engineer

  • You actually write code. TypeScript is our stack; you should be comfortable enough to build a working integration live on a call without rehearsing it first

  • You know APIs deeply — OpenAPI, JSON Schema, auth flows, SDK ergonomics, and what separates a reference doc that works from one that just exists

  • A function that currently exists only in the founder's head reads as the reason to take the job rather than the reason to pass

  • You can take a deal from first technical call to signed to successfully onboarded without being handed a process for it

  • You'd rather be honest about a limitation and win the next deal than talk around it

  • You'd rather collaborate to the right answer than win the argument, and you operate with a high level of kindness

Nice to have

  • Experience at a developer-tools or API company, especially selling to engineering teams

  • Hands-on with MCP, agents, or LLM-powered developer tooling — we're building on the MCP SDK, the Vercel AI SDK, and Vertex AI

  • Vue 3, or comfort ramping into it quickly

  • You've been the first or second GTM technical hire somewhere and know what that actually costs

  • Experience running technical evaluations against enterprise requirements — self-hosting, SSO/SAML, air-gapped deployments, procurement security reviews

  • An in-house-first instinct — we build our own clients and tooling and work hard to reduce external dependencies

  • Open-source contributions we can go read

Where we work

In-office in San Francisco. Scalar is otherwise a remote team, and our engineering roles are remote — but we're building the sales team in person on purpose. You'll be in a room with Marc and two SDRs, every day, in the year where we scale the sales organization.

That's the real offer here. Founder-led sales is learned by sitting next to the founder while he does it — hearing the call that goes sideways, watching which technical objection actually kills a deal, arguing about the pricing conversation on the walk back. None of that survives being written down or watched later in a recording. Expect meaningful in-person time with customers and prospects around the Bay Area too.

We offer flexible, unlimited time off. We believe prioritizing the team's well-being makes the work better and more meaningful.

Other notes

  • While the role is customer-facing, you'll be in the codebase regularly and may be asked to own a feature end to end where it unblocks a customer.

  • We are a small team of ten and wear many hats. We expect everyone to pitch in and help out where needed.

  • This role has a variable component tied to team and company targets, not an individual quota — you should be optimizing for customers succeeding, not for closing something that shouldn't close.

  • Compensation Range: $145,000–$185,000 (USD) base plus variable, for an on-target range of $170,000–$215,000, based on experience — plus meaningful early equity.

title: Retail Assistant - (Fixed-Term Ending 10/01/27)
description:
Welcome to Warner Bros. Discovery… the stuff dreams are made of.

Who We Are…

When we say, “the stuff dreams are made of,” we’re not just referring to the world of wizards, dragons and superheroes, or even to the wonders of Planet Earth. Behind WBD’s vast portfolio of iconic content and beloved brands, are the storytellers bringing our characters to life, the creators bringing them to your living rooms and the dreamers creating what’s next…

From brilliant creatives, to technology trailblazers, across the globe, WBD offers career defining opportunities, thoughtfully curated benefits, and the tools to explore and grow into your best selves. Here you are supported, here you are celebrated, here you can thrive.

Your New Role

Oxford Street is about to become home to a flagship shop that redefines the retail experience. Our official Harry Potter Shop will blend iconic storytelling with world‑class retail standards, creating a destination that delights fans from around the world.

We’re looking for enthusiastic and customer‑focused Retail Associates to bring this experience to life on the shopfloor every day. In this role, you’ll be the face of the store — welcoming customers, delivering memorable service and working at pace to keep the shop running smoothly during busy trading periods.

Harry Potter Shop Oxford Street sits alongside world‑class attractions and retail experiences including Warner Bros. Studio Tour London, Warner Bros. Studio Tour Tokyo, Harry Potter Shop King’s Cross, and flagship stores in New York, Chicago and Harajuku.

Your Role Accountabilities:

  • Deliver warm, friendly and engaging customer service, ensuring every visitor feels welcomed and valued.

  • Create memorable, personalised experiences that inspire customers to return again and again.

  • Engage customers confidently, offering product knowledge and assistance to support their visit.

  • Maintain high shopfloor standards, ensuring products are well presented and the environment is clean and inviting.

  • Work with pace and efficiency to replenish stock and maintain product availability throughout the day.

  • Support back‑of‑house activity, including delivery processing, stock organisation and replenishment.

  • Adapt quickly to changing priorities during busy periods, remaining calm and positive at all times.

  • Follow all health & safety, loss prevention and cash handling procedures.


Skills and Qualifications

Passion for delivering great customer service.
Positive, friendly and enthusiastic attitude.
Ability to work at pace whilst maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
Strong teamwork and communication skills.
Comfortable working in a fast‑paced, customer‑facing environment.
Willingness to work across shopfloor and back‑of‑house areas.
Retail experience is helpful but not essential — full training will be provided.

Working Pattern

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), fixed-term position (ending 10th January 2027), on a seven-day rota including weekends and Bank Holidays.
Working hours are between 7am and 10pm.

Before applying, please ensure you are available to attend our Assessment Centre in London on 11 September 2026, as attendance is a mandatory part of the selection process.

#RETAILHP

Onsite Working - This role is advertised as Onsite, meaning all working hours and days (regardless of shift pattern) will be carried out at the place of work. Subject to any applicable laws, WBD / your Line Manager reserves the right to change this working agreement, where this is essential to business needs and upon reasonable notice to you.

How We Get Things Done…

This last bit is probably the most important! Here at WBD, our guiding principles are the core values by which we operate and are central to how we get things done. You can find them at along with some insights from the team on what they mean and how they show up in their day to day. We hope they resonate with you and look forward to discussing them during your interview.

Championing Inclusion at WBD

Warner Bros. Discovery embraces the opportunity to build a workforce that reflects a wide array of perspectives, backgrounds and experiences. Being an equal opportunity employer means that we take seriously our responsibility to consider qualified candidates on the basis of merit, regardless of sex, gender identity, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion or belief, marital status, pregnancy, parenthood, disability or any other category protected by law.

If you’re a qualified candidate with a disability and you require adjustments or accommodations during the job application and/or recruitment process, please visit our accessibility page for instructions to submit your request.

title: Senior Director Client Services
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Director Client Services based in the United States.

This is an executive-level client services leadership role focused on delivering exceptional outcomes across complex benefits administration programs.
You will set the direction for client service excellence while strengthening long-term partnerships and supporting business growth.
The role combines strategic client leadership with hands-on oversight of service delivery, operational performance, and team development.
You will work closely with project management, production planning, customer success, sales, and other cross-functional teams to ensure priorities are aligned and execution is strong.
As a senior escalation point, you will identify risks, resolve complex service challenges, and translate performance data into actionable recommendations.
You will also help shape renewal, cross-sell, and new-business opportunities while developing high-performing client services professionals.
The environment values collaboration, continuous learning, technology, security, and a strong commitment to client satisfaction.

Accountabilities

  • Lead the strategic direction and day-to-day management of major client service engagements, ensuring service quality, performance, and client satisfaction remain consistently high.
  • Partner with Project Management and Production Planning to review capacity, deliverables, performance, work requests, and resource allocation.
  • Monitor client health scorecards, identify emerging risks, and work with teams to develop and implement corrective actions.
  • Serve as a senior escalation point for service delivery concerns, ensuring issues are documented, addressed, and resolved effectively.
  • Provide regular operational performance reporting to client leadership, highlighting achievements, risks, priorities, and resource needs.
  • Lead strategy discussions with Customer Success and internal stakeholders to assess client activity, business needs, performance, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Establish effective team operating rhythms, including stand-ups, regular one-to-ones, performance reviews, and ongoing communication around business priorities.
  • Coach, mentor, and develop Client Services team members while supporting onboarding, training, learning paths, and resource planning.
  • Oversee Annual Enrollment activities, proactively coordinating with clients and internal teams to ensure milestones and outstanding items are successfully managed.
  • Partner with Sales on finalist meetings, prospective client visits, scope-of-services presentations, renewals, cross-sell opportunities, and broader account growth initiatives.
  • Maintain strong knowledge of product releases, technology developments, system functionality, and benefits administration trends to provide informed client guidance.
  • Uphold organizational policies, operational standards, security practices, and privacy requirements while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

    • Requirements

    • Bachelor's degree in Management, Communications, or a related discipline.
    • 8+ years of progressive experience working with brokers, carriers, and clients within the benefits administration industry.
    • Strong experience in Health & Welfare benefits, healthcare, Human Resources, benefits technology, or a closely related environment.
    • Proven expertise in client relationship management, with the ability to establish trust, influence stakeholders, and serve as a senior strategic advisor.
    • Strong project and operational management skills, including the ability to coordinate complex priorities across multiple teams.
    • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with a resourceful and creative approach to resolving client and operational challenges.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with confidence engaging executives, clients, team members, and cross-functional stakeholders.
    • Proven people leadership experience, including coaching, mentoring, performance management, training, and team development.
    • Strong commercial awareness and the ability to contribute to sales opportunities, renewals, cross-selling, and client growth strategies.
    • Technology fluency and a willingness to learn and communicate effectively about modern platforms, products, and system functionality.
    • Highly motivated, confident, energetic, and positive, with a collaborative leadership style and a strong commitment to continuous learning.
    • Willingness and ability to travel up to 15% as required.

      • Benefits

      • Annual salary range of $110,000–$172,000, depending on education, experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, internal equity, and market factors.
      • Eligibility to participate in a quarterly bonus incentive plan.
      • Comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees.
      • Flexible and remote work environment.
      • Opportunities for professional development, continuous learning, and career growth.
      • Collaborative culture focused on client success, innovation, and employee development.
      • Opportunities to expand expertise across benefits technology, healthcare, HR, and related areas.

title: Structural Dynamics Engineer
description:
Be a part of our mission! As a world leader in creating comfortable, sustainable, and efficient climate solutions for buildings, homes and transportation, it's our responsibility to put the planet first. For us at Trane Technologies, and through our businesses including Trane® and Thermo King, sustainability is not just how we do business—it is our business. Do you dare to look at the world's challenges and see impactful possibilities? Do you want to contribute to making a better future? If the answer is yes, we invite you to consider joining us in boldly challenging what's possible for a sustainable world.

Learn about our benefits designed for you to Thrive at work and at home.

We boldly go.

Where is the work:

Monday to Thursday, work onsite with your colleagues. Fridays, choose your work location, balancing what your work requires.

As a Structural Dynamics Engineer at Trane, you will be responsible for designing the equipment and systems that support these goals. You will work with engineering teams, develop concepts for new & improved commercial HVAC products and help solve complex technical problems, leading to production of sustainable new products.

Join a team that applies experimental and computational methods to develop best-in-class Trane Commercial HVAC products and enabling technologies while addressing acoustic, structural & vibration challenges. The primary focus areas of this Structural Dynamics Engineer role include structural integrity, structural dynamics, vibration simulation and testing. Work closely with various product and technology development teams and with global Engineering support center personnel.


Core Job Responsibilities (others may be added):

  • Lead and carry out the advancement of the Acoustics & Mechanics Engineering function. The scope encompasses technology in both computational and experimental tools and methodologies applicable to Commercial HVAC products.

  • Plan, conduct, and supervise work related to developing structural and structural dynamic simulation models. The scope includes prediction of structural modes, dynamic response, stress, strain, deformation, fatigue, etc. using finite element (FEA) and/or other methods.

  • Plan, conduct, and supervise various structural and structural dynamic tests, including but not limited to, structural modal analysis, steady state and transient vibration, rotating machinery, strength tests, component fatigue, data collection and analysis.

  • Correlating simulation or any other prediction models with test data to improve prediction accuracy and validate models.

  • Develop and improve standard work and design guidelines related to, but not limited to, structural design, simulation, testing, and similar work.

  • Work closely with product engineers to design reliable and durable products.

  • Work closely with test engineers and technicians. Responsibilities include understanding and prioritizing test requests, designing and proposing the appropriate test, discussing and supervising test implementations, assuring the validity of the data and its interpretation, and documenting the work in formal reports.

  • Act as a member of the various product and technology development teams to design reliable and durable products.

  • Support and successfully accomplish annual corporate objectives for individuals and teams.

  • Effectively utilize personal project management techniques and utilize the available technical skills and resources necessary for success.

  • Work closely with and mentor other engineering resources globally.

  • Some overnight travel will be required (probably less than 10%).


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering (or related discipline) and at least 2-years of work experience in structural dynamics is required.

  • Master's Degree is a plus.


Key Skills or Competencies:

  • Formal coursework in mechanics of materials, vibration, structural dynamics, numerical simulation methods, digital signal processing is expected.

  • Experience with ANSYS, Siemens SimCenter or Siemens Test.Lab is a plus.

  • Experience in structural engineering design, technical problem-solving with simulation and tests.

  • Knowledge in the design, testing, and optimization for dynamics of machinery.

  • Knowledge and experience in correlating simulation models and test data are a plus.

  • Strong teamwork, interpersonal, communication and project management skills required.

  • Must be able to work on multiple high-priority projects simultaneously.

  • Experience in data acquisition systems, both hardware and software, as well as mechanical strain measurement, are preferred.

  • Experience with HVAC products, compressors, fans and sheet metal structures is a plus.

$84,740.00 - $118,860.00

No

title: Senior Technical Program Manager (Cloud Capacity)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager (Cloud Capacity) based in Germany.

Join a fast-growing technical organization building infrastructure for the global AI economy and large-scale cloud workloads.
You’ll own capacity planning and expansion across multiple data centers, ensuring infrastructure keeps pace with customer demand.
Working at the intersection of data analytics, infrastructure engineering, procurement, operations, and product, you’ll turn consumption trends into concrete infrastructure requirements.
You’ll analyze usage patterns, build forecasts, identify capacity risks, and coordinate expansions from initial planning through customer availability.
The role combines hands-on quantitative analysis with complex program management across independent technical and business teams.
Your decisions will directly influence infrastructure readiness, resource availability, operational efficiency, and the ability to scale cloud services reliably.
This is an ideal opportunity for a data-driven technical program leader who enjoys solving complex capacity challenges and taking ownership from forecast to execution.

Accountabilities

  • Analyze historical and current consumption of cloud resources to identify trends, anomalies, demand patterns, and potential capacity constraints.
  • Build and maintain capacity forecasts for compute, storage, and other infrastructure resources across multiple data centers.
  • Translate demand forecasts into concrete infrastructure requirements, including the number and type of additional servers and resources needed.
  • Initiate capacity requests and work closely with Supply Chain teams throughout procurement, purchasing, delivery, and deployment.
  • Maintain an end-to-end view of capacity expansion projects, from demand forecasting and requirements definition through procurement, delivery, installation, deployment, and customer availability.
  • Coordinate expansion plans with data center operations teams, including installation schedules, infrastructure readiness, and deployment dependencies.
  • Work closely with engineering teams to plan and coordinate the deployment of new capacity.
  • Track project timelines, dependencies, risks, and blockers while proactively driving resolution across teams.
  • Provide engineering, product, business, and leadership stakeholders with clear and reliable information about capacity plans, delivery timelines, current status, risks, and dependencies.
  • Take ownership of capacity-related outcomes by anticipating upcoming challenges, driving decisions, following up on commitments, and ensuring issues are resolved rather than passed between teams.
  • Continuously improve capacity planning processes, analytical approaches, reporting, and operational workflows.

    • Requirements

    • Proven experience in technical project or program management, data analytics, capacity planning, infrastructure planning, or a closely related field.
    • Strong analytical background with the ability to work confidently with quantitative data and use it to guide operational and strategic decisions.
    • Understanding of fundamental statistical concepts and forecasting methodologies, including their practical limitations and appropriate use cases.
    • Ability to understand technical infrastructure constraints and communicate effectively with engineers and technical specialists.
    • Demonstrated experience coordinating complex work across multiple independent teams without relying on formal authority.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical and analytical information into clear plans, decisions, risks, timelines, and status updates for different audiences.
    • Strong ownership mindset, with a proactive approach to identifying risks, driving decisions, following up on actions, and delivering outcomes.
    • Excellent organizational and prioritization skills, particularly when managing multiple dependencies and competing capacity requirements.
    • Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities, forecasts, and infrastructure needs can evolve.
    • Previous experience as a data analyst, product analyst, or similar analytical role before transitioning into program or project management is a strong advantage.
    • Ability to independently query and analyze data using SQL is a plus.
    • Hands-on experience with monitoring and business intelligence tools such as Grafana, DataLens, or similar platforms is desirable.
    • Experience with capacity planning, demand forecasting, infrastructure resource management, or cloud resource optimization is highly valued.
    • Understanding of cloud or data center infrastructure, including servers, racks, compute, storage, networking, and operational dependencies, is a strong advantage.
    • Experience with procurement, hardware supply chains, or physical infrastructure deployments is a plus.

      • Benefits

      • Competitive compensation.
      • Career growth and continuous learning opportunities.
      • Flexible working environment with significant ownership and autonomy.
      • Opportunity to work remotely from Germany as part of a Europe-based team.
      • International environment with talented engineers, technical specialists, and business professionals.
      • Opportunity to work on impactful infrastructure projects supporting the rapidly growing AI ecosystem.
      • Exposure to large-scale cloud capacity planning, data center operations, infrastructure engineering, and supply chain processes.
      • Opportunity to influence how infrastructure is planned, scaled, and made available to customers.
      • Fast-moving culture that encourages bold thinking, continuous growth, and meaningful impact.
      • Strong emphasis on trust, ownership, and the opportunity to shape the future of AI.
      • Inclusive workplace committed to equal employment opportunities and a diverse workforce.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

Senior Software Engineer UK

Full-time /London (Engineering)

About Applied Intuition Defence

Applied Intuition UK is a software and infrastructure supplier that accelerates the deployment of next-generation autonomous capabilities to the warfighter across air, land, sea, and space. A subsidiary of Applied Intuition, we deliver dual-use solutions to national security customers that build upon several years of product development and experience from commercial autonomy programs. Based in London, our seasoned defence team hails from Palantir, Anduril, SpaceX, Google, Lockheed Martin, and the UK and US Armed Services. Learn more at appliedintuitiondefense.com.

About the role

As a senior software engineer on the UK engineering team, your day-to-day activities will vary. Somedays you might find yourself in the field, working alongside our forward deployment team integrating with customer platforms and technologies, other days you might be leading the design on a brand-new product to satisfy the requirements of various different customers and partners that we work with. Every day is different, and each day is exciting. You are given the opportunity to showcase the skills you’ve learned during your career, and teach the more junior members of the team. You will build, test and deploy your software and watch it actually be used.

At Applied Intuition, you will:

  • Lead the design, development, and optimization of new tools and products, taking them through from incubation all the way to production

  • Spot the ineffectiveness of the processes and code you work with daily to ensure the team are always working to the best of their abilities

  • Integrate software from customers and other teams into the products we are making

  • Write, test, and debug efficient modern C++ code for complex software solutions with the help of AI tooling

  • Work closely with product managers and customers to understand requirements and translate them into technical solutions

  • Train and mentor junior engineers as we grow the UK team, fostering a culture of learning and improvement

  • Build awesome software that you are proud of

We’re looking for someone who has:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science/related engineering field

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience developing performant modern C++, or high willingness to learn C++ which is our primary programming language for all development

  • Strong procedural and object-oriented programming experience that employs clean code principles and good OOP design patterns/principles

  • Experience developing in Docker and containerized development environments, and using Linux-based operating systems

Travel Requirements:

  • General willingness to travel for company business between our offices, as well as to customer sites

Security Requirements:

  • Must have ability to hold UK Security Clearance (current or previous preferred)

Nice to have:

  • 7+ years of experience developing software in modern C++ and Python

  • Experience working on distributed systems, with simulation technology and autonomy

  • Experience with Bazel, Nix and other similar technologies

  • Experience deploying to, and working with infrastructure technologies

  • Experience working projects related to national security for one or more government agencies

  • References who will describe them as low-ego, highly motivated, thoughtfully opinionated, strong communicators and curious listeners

title: Real Property Analyst
description:
Position Title: Real Property Analyst

Reports to: Operations Manager

Location: Fort Buchanan, PR

Work Schedule: Full-Time, Monday – Friday

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt


Position Summary: Aldevra is currently seeking a qualified Real Property Analyst to support the United States Army Reserve (USAR) in Fort Buchanan, PR. We are looking for someone who brings a positive attitude, strong attention to detail, clear communication, and a willingness to jump in where needed. The right person will also connect with Aldevra’s core values of SOAR: Strong Integrity and Ethics, Outstanding Teamwork, Accountability-Driven, and Relentless Pursuit of Quality.


This position is contingent upon contract award.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The essential functions include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Support a distributed, forward deployed Real Property execution model in which contractor personnel are embedded at designated Readiness Divisions (RDs), the 9th Mission Support Command (MSC), and Army Reserve Funded Installations (ARFIs).
  • Embedded personnel shall provide daily technical execution support to local Realty staff while reporting strategically to the USARC G-3/5/7 Engineers Directorate, which serves as the Accountable Organization for Army Reserve real property.
  • Shall coordinate daily activities with local DPW Realty staff and shall submit standardized monthly reports directly to the USARC G-3/5/7 Engineers Directorate to ensure the Accountable Organization maintains visibility of real property execution across all supported locations.
  • Work directly with Realty staff at the local Directorate of Public Works (DPW) to execute day-to-day real property transactions. This includes updating the General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS) with acquisitions, disposals, and capital improvements.
  • Plan and execute physical inventories of real property assets within their assigned installation/region footprint in accordance with (IAW) Army Regulation (AR) 405-45.
  • Identify "found on site" assets, research historical documentation (such as as-builts and transfer memos), and prepare DD Form 1354s for capitalization.
  • Submit a Monthly Status Report (MSR) directly to the USARC G3/5/7 Engineers Directorate Real Property Branch.
  • Prepare "Health Check" briefings for USARC leadership regarding the real property status of their assigned Readiness Division (RD)/Army Reserve Functional Installation (ARFI).
  • Execute USARC’s phased remediation model to address identified InSITE discrepancies.
  • Support remediation of approximately 625 critical issues across 191 sites, prioritizing assets per USARC direction (>$1M or as directed). Phase 1 shall address administrative fixes (UIC mismatches, FAC/CATCODE corrections, historic status, disposal status) primarily via desktop actions. Phase 2 shall address substantive fixes requiring multi-step validation and on-site measurements to correct quantity errors (square footage/acreage) and verify sustainment and operational status.
  • Provide a monthly InSITE Progress Report included in the MSR. Surge Support and Special Missions (Fly-Away Capability) The Contractor shall maintain a fly-away Mobile Support Team capability to provide surge support, audits, and urgent inventories at locations outside assigned duty stations upon direction of the COR.
  • Reconcile the Universe of Transactions (UoT), resolve Unmatched Transactions (UMTs), and correct Intermediate Document (IDOC) failures between GFEBS and HQIIS (Headquarters Installation Information System), and shall provide weekly exception logs and corrective action plans to the COR.
  • Provide support for HQDA and USARC Real Property-related taskers, G-4 Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) sample testing, and Army audit submissions. This includes assisting in the retrieval and preparation of documentation to address instances of non-submittal or constraints in obtaining required paperwork.
  • All other duties as assigned.

About Us

Aldevra was founded in 2009 by current President & CEO Rodney Marshall, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and minority entrepreneur. The company began by selling foodservice equipment to the federal government and later expanded to include medical equipment and professional services, helping to meet a broader range of customer needs. Today, Aldevra is recognized as a top foodservice equipment dealer in the U.S., specializing in federal government sales while also growing its commercial and e-commerce customer base. Its professional services division provides federal agencies with healthcare professionals, construction and facilities managers and technicians, and administrative support. Whether it's equipment or staffing, Aldevra is committed to delivering high-quality products and timely service at the best value.


Recent accolades include:

  • Great Place to Work®
  • 2026 Military Friendly® Employer Gold designation
  • 2025 HIRE Vets Medallion Award
  • VETS Indexes 5-Star Employer for 2026 Employer Awards
  • Department of Defense Military Spouse Employment Partnership Small Business Partner
  • Army Partnership for Your Success (PaYS) Partner #911
  • Foodservice Equipment & Supplies magazine 2026 Distribution Giants list
  • Foodservice Equipment Reports 2025 Top Dealer
  • RATIONAL 2025 Premium Partner Award
  • ENERGY STAR® Partner

Learn more about us at aldevra.com.

title: Senior Software Engineer, MediaWiki Content Platform Team
description:

You’ll design and deliver systems used by hundreds of millions of people and collaborate with engineers, product managers, designers, client teams, and community contributors.

  • Develop and maintain PHP and JavaScript software supporting content experiences across hundreds of languages.
  • Design, implement, and maintain reliable internet-facing APIs using appropriate server-side technologies.
  • Build and improve components that are performant, maintainable, and consumed by other teams, products, and large numbers of users.
  • Instrument systems and components to monitor performance, quality, reliability, and feature characteristics.
  • Leverage caching and persistence technologies to improve the scalability and responsiveness of content services.
  • Make and communicate architectural decisions while navigating ambiguity and balancing competing technical trade-offs.
  • Contribute to strong engineering practices through unit and integration testing, code reviews, security improvements, documentation, and maintainability initiatives.
  • Mentor other engineers through technical discussions, code reviews, documentation, and direct guidance, helping raise the technical quality of the wider team.

    • Requirements

    • 5+ years of relevant professional software engineering experience, with a track record of delivering production software at meaningful scale.
    • Experience with one or more areas such as parser generators, interpreters, language runtimes, compilers, or taking language features through a complete product lifecycle.
    • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex technical projects, make architectural decisions, communicate trade-offs, and deliver outcomes with limited direction.
    • Experience designing and maintaining reliable, high-performance software components used by other teams, products, or large user populations.

    • A history of open-source contributions is a strong advantage.
    • A bachelor's, master's, or doctorate degree in computer science, software engineering, STEM, or equivalent professional certification is welcome but not essential.
