title: Warehouse Operative
description:
Welcome to Warner Bros. Discovery… the stuff dreams are made of.

Who We Are…

When we say, “the stuff dreams are made of,” we’re not just referring to the world of wizards, dragons and superheroes, or even to the wonders of Planet Earth. Behind WBD’s vast portfolio of iconic content and beloved brands, are the storytellers bringing our characters to life, the creators bringing them to your living rooms and the dreamers creating what’s next…

From brilliant creatives, to technology trailblazers, across the globe, WBD offers career defining opportunities, thoughtfully curated benefits, and the tools to explore and grow into your best selves. Here you are supported, here you are celebrated, here you can thrive.

Your New Role

As a Warehouse Operative, you will support warehouse and ecommerce activities across Warner Bros. Tours & Retail. You will help ensure stock is handled accurately, orders are prepared to a high standard, and customers receive a dependable service.

You will contribute to stock management, order fulfilment, and maintaining a safe, organised warehouse environment. If you are looking for a role where attention to detail and teamwork make a real impact, apply today.

What’s in it for you?

  • £15.76 per hour

  • Opportunity for full FTL certification

  • 25 days holiday, pro-rata

  • GymPass

  • Exclusive access to our Screeners App, featuring Warner Bros. and HBO content

  • Discounted tickets for the tour

  • Free tickets for family and friends on selected days, up to 8 tickets

  • Option to join our pension and private healthcare schemes

Your Role Accountabilities...

  • Receive, check, and accept deliveries, maintaining accurate records and ensuring stock is correctly stored and replenished, including use of machinery where required.

  • Pick and pack orders for stores and ecommerce customers, ensuring accuracy, correct product selection, and high presentation standards including personalisation where needed.

  • Maintain warehouse organisation, cleanliness, and stock control, minimising loss through careful handling and housekeeping.

  • Monitor and report stock issues, order discrepancies, as well as equipment or vehicle defects to support service quality and operational efficiency.

  • Support distribution by preparing and delivering stock to retail outlets, including London locations where required.

  • Follow Health & Safety policies, participate in daily briefings, and contribute to a safe working environment.

  • Maintain accurate warehouse administration, support stock counts, and complete tasks requested by the Warehouse Management Team.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Prior experience in a warehouse, ecommerce, or transferable environment, e.g. retail or logistics.

  • Comfortable working at height; full training and equipment will be provided.

  • Ability to prioritise tasks, use initiative, and meet deadlines.

  • Reliability and flexibility, particularly during peak trading periods.

  • Experience with warehouse systems or machinery is beneficial; full training is provided.

  • Full UK Driving License

Working Pattern…

  • 40-hour working week, in a shift pattern from Monday to Sunday, with varying start and finish times between 7am and 8pm. This also includes working Bank Holidays.

  • You will be required to work 1 in every 3 weekends, however this is subject to change during peak times i.e. every other weekend

  • No night work required, but evening work will be required

#T&R

Onsite Working - This role is advertised as Onsite, meaning all working hours and days (regardless of shift pattern) will be carried out at the place of work. Subject to any applicable laws, WBD / your Line Manager reserves the right to change this working agreement, where this is essential to business needs and upon reasonable notice to you.

How We Get Things Done…

This last bit is probably the most important! Here at WBD, our guiding principles are the core values by which we operate and are central to how we get things done. You can find them at along with some insights from the team on what they mean and how they show up in their day to day. We hope they resonate with you and look forward to discussing them during your interview.

Championing Inclusion at WBD

Warner Bros. Discovery embraces the opportunity to build a workforce that reflects a wide array of perspectives, backgrounds and experiences. Being an equal opportunity employer means that we take seriously our responsibility to consider qualified candidates on the basis of merit, regardless of sex, gender identity, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion or belief, marital status, pregnancy, parenthood, disability or any other category protected by law.

If you’re a qualified candidate with a disability and you require adjustments or accommodations during the job application and/or recruitment process, please visit our accessibility page for instructions to submit your request.

title: Territory Director
description:
The Territory Director provides leadership for the supply chain operations within an assigned area of the distribution network. This position is accountable for achieving company objectives, performance standards, and operating expense goals at multiple distribution centers within a defined geographical territory within North America. The incumbent is responsible for the overall servicing of customers within the territory, as well as the overall management and performance of the warehouse facilities within the region including warehouse operations, customer relations, quality, safety, and security.

Key Responsibilities & Duties:

  • Develops and directs all Managers to ensure efficient and cost-effective warehouse operations.
  • Oversees all distribution services including receiving, storing, shipping, handling returned/damaged product, and administrative duties to ensure customer requirements are met.
  • Develops and executes account planning strategies to increase sales by maintaining or growing existing business as well as capitalizing on new business.
  • Accountable to achieve all metrics associated with each warehouse facility; directs the operations of warehouse managers to achieve prescribed objectives.
  • Recruits, hires, and trains a productive warehouse management team; matches the skill and background of candidates to the work required.
  • Monitors space layout plan at each warehouse to ensure it continues to meet company standards.
  • Directs programs to ensure the safety of all employees, equipment, and property.
  • Monitor the safety performance of the warehouse facilities to ensure all work-related injuries are immediately reported in compliance with EH&S processes.
  • Ensure compliance with appropriate government regulations.
  • Maintains a professional relationship with all customers.
  • Audits operations to ensure service and safety standards are being met.
  • Ensure accurate inventory control for product.
  • Ensure the security of the warehouse facilities.
  • Participates in Labor contract negotiations as requested.
  • Assumes other duties as assigned.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • BS Degree required and at least five (5) years in a regional distribution leadership role.
  • A strong background in warehouse operations.
  • Working knowledge of warehouse and transportation management systems.
  • Must be able to effectively communicate within the organization and business units throughout the company, and with partners across the supply chain.
  • Must value diversity and exhibit a leadership style that creates a cohesive team environment.
  • Must be successful in managing effective deployment of resources to achieve organizational objectives.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements:

  • Based out of the incumbent's home office, the Regional Distribution Director is required to travel up to 70% of the time, and during travel is exposed to an industrial warehouse and customer environment which may include working near moving mechanical machinery with a high noise level and hot and cold climate based on weather.
  • Minimal physical effort is required. Work is mostly sedentary, but does require walking, standing, bending, reaching, and very occasionally lifting or carrying objects that weigh up to 50 lbs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Six Sigma Certification Desired.

Benefits & Compensation:

  • Competitive salary
  • Comprehensive benefit package, including Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid time off and paid holidays
  • Employer Paid Life insurance and long-term disability
  • Parental leave and continuing education support

title: VP of Brand
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a VP of Brand based in the United States.

This is a high-impact leadership opportunity to define and elevate the next chapter of a fast-growing consumer brand.
You will own brand strategy, storytelling, positioning, creative direction, and cultural relevance from strategy through execution.
The role sits at the intersection of consumer insight, product truth, creativity, and commercial growth.
You will shape how the brand appears across DTC, retail, packaging, content, social, partnerships, and customer experiences.
You will also build and lead a high-performing Brand organization spanning creative, content, community, partnerships, and activations.
With significant autonomy and direct executive access, you will raise creative standards while building the systems and talent needed to scale.
This role is ideal for a commercially minded brand builder who wants to create something distinctive, memorable, and enduring.

Accountabilities

  • Define brand strategy and positioning: Translate consumer insights, product strengths, and competitive dynamics into a clear target customer, differentiated positioning, value proposition, messaging hierarchy, and compelling launch narratives.
  • Lead brand storytelling across channels: Ensure the brand story is consistently and creatively expressed across packaging, digital, retail, organic content, communications, launches, and the broader customer experience.
  • Build cultural relevance and community: Develop organic content, creator and influencer relationships, partnerships, events, activations, and community programs that strengthen participation, awareness, and brand affinity.
  • Establish brand standards: Own and evolve the brand strategy, voice, identity, creative direction, and standards to create a distinctive and recognizable presence across customer touchpoints.
  • Build the Brand organization: Recruit, develop, and lead a high-performing team across creative, organic social, content, community, partnerships, and activations, while establishing effective agency and partner relationships.
  • Drive annual brand planning: Own the annual brand plan, marketing calendar, awareness budget, campaign priorities, and investment decisions in alignment with broader commercial objectives.
  • Raise creative and operational performance: Establish a higher creative bar while improving speed, reducing rework, and creating an operating model that enables teams and partners to execute effectively.
  • Connect brand to business growth: Use consumer insight, data, and commercial judgment to prioritize initiatives that build awareness, preference, participation, and measurable business impact.

    • Requirements

    • Senior brand leadership experience: Significant experience leading brand functions within a high-growth consumer business, ideally in CPG, health, wellness, performance, or a closely related category.
    • Exceptional storytelling and positioning: Demonstrated ability to turn consumer insight, product truth, and competitive context into compelling propositions, narratives, and launches that contribute to product and business success.
    • Proven brand-building track record: Experience developing distinctive brands and leading integrated campaigns, activations, communications, and experiences with measurable impact.
    • Strong creative judgment: Ability to set a high creative standard and effectively direct designers, writers, content teams, agencies, and other creative partners without needing to be the primary creator.
    • Team-building leadership: Proven ability to build and lead high-performing teams, establish clear standards, and improve both quality and execution speed.
    • Omnichannel expertise: Experience across direct-to-consumer, retail, packaging, product launches, digital channels, and broader consumer experiences.
    • Commercial and analytical mindset: Ability to use consumer insights and data to inform decisions while balancing analysis with strong judgment, creativity, and decisive action.
    • Executive presence and ownership: Comfortable operating with autonomy in a fast-moving, founder-led environment where candor, resourcefulness, accountability, and initiative are highly valued.
    • Strategic and operational versatility: Able to move fluidly between setting long-term brand direction, making investment decisions, challenging creative work, and building the organization required to execute the strategy.

      • Benefits

      • Competitive base salary: $180,000–$235,000 USD annually, with the final offer determined by experience, skills, and local market conditions.
      • Performance opportunity: Eligibility for performance bonuses in addition to base compensation.
      • Remote flexibility: Fully remote position open to candidates based in the United States.
      • Meaningful ownership: Significant responsibility for brand strategy, team development, creative direction, and the initiatives shaping the next stage of growth.
      • Executive access: Direct access to company leadership and the opportunity to influence major strategic and creative decisions.
      • Growth environment: Join a scaled, high-growth consumer business where the brand-building opportunity remains substantial.
      • Professional development: Benefits and opportunities designed to support health, wellness, and professional growth.

title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer - Spacecraft
description:
Please Note: To conform with the United States Government Space Technology Export Regulations, the applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., conditional resident, asylee or refugee (protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
At CesiumAstro, we are developers and pioneers of out-of-the-box communication systems for satellites, UAVs, launch vehicles, and other space and airborne platforms. We take pride in our dynamic and cross-functional work environment, which allows us to learn, develop, and engage across our organization. If you are looking for hands-on, interactive, and autonomous work, CesiumAstro is the place for you. We are actively seeking passionate, collaborative, energetic, and forward-thinking individuals to join our team.

We are looking to add a Senior Flight Software Engineer to our Internal Missions team. If you enjoy working in a startup environment and are passionate about developing software for leading-edge communications satellites, we would like to hear from you.
In this position, you will be responsible for the CesiumAstro satellite flight software and software-in-the-loop testing through all stages of the development process. Your work will include developing software to monitor, test, and control spacecraft subsystems such as attitude, command and data handling, navigation, thermal, and power. The ideal candidate will be an experienced spacecraft software engineer, motivated to develop every aspect of space mission software from Linux-based satellite operating systems to low-level embedded products. You will work and learn from a cohort of senior and principal software engineers. You will use your experience to direct, mentor, and grow a team of motivated spacecraft engineers in the development of a new satellite system.
As a CesiumAstro team member, you will work on a small team to develop satellites and put them in orbit. You will be responsible for software design to include initial architecture and block diagrams, requirements definition, implementation, code review, and validation and verification. You will need to identify simplifying solutions to simulate complex problems and explain key results and decisions to the team.

  • Review code and system designs.

  • Integrate and validate new product designs.
  • Support software quality assurance and optimize I/O performance.
  • Provide post-production/in-orbit customer support.
  • Interface with hardware design and development engineers.
  • Assess third party and open-source software.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor of Science (BS), Master of Science (MS), or Doctorate (PhD) degree in Software or Computer Engineering from an accredited university or institution.
  • Minimum of 5 years of industry experience in spacecraft software development. A Master's degree may count as two years of experience.
  • Experience in hands-on development and troubleshooting of software systems and hardware (such as motors, power distribution units, etc.).
  • Experience with C, C++, Python, or other languages in an aerospace context.
  • A strong understanding of space missions from conception through flight and disposal.
  • Familiarity with spacecraft mission design including events, pointing modes, maneuver planning, sequencing, and operations.
  • Experience with spacecraft failure in post-CDR testing and on-orbit, root cause analysis, and recovery.
  • Experience with design for reliability, spaceflight redundancy, and fault detection, identification, and recovery.
  • Space software experience with attitude dynamics, coordinate frame transformations, vector mathematics, radiative heat transfer, spacecraft propulsion, space communication systems, and power systems.
  • Experience with communication protocols such as TCP/IP or UDP for use in software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop lab development and for use in space flight.
  • Experience in interfacing a variety of open-source software to create an integrated system.
  • Embedded software experience, particularly for space missions.
  • Ability to implement physical first principles as scripts or spreadsheets.
  • Experience with processes for software release, revisioning, and configuration.
  • Familiarity with configuration management tools, defect tracking tools, and peer review.
  • Experience with trades and processes for handling radiation tolerance in software on automotive grade parts.
  • Familiarity with systems for continuous integration, test, and delivery.
  • Excellent understanding of multi-threaded applications and resource management.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

  • CubeSat and SmallSat experience including LEO, MEO, GEO, and beyond.
  • Hands-on experience with spacecraft instrumentation, subsystems, and test labs.
  • Experience with JPL F’, NASA cFS, and other commercial space software frameworks.
  • Experience with ground system software engineering for space missions.
  • Experience in a team leadership role on a space software program.
  • Experience in other non-space safety critical software programs.
  • Experience with network security.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Engineering · Amsterdam (hybrid)

Inner Circle is a dating app for people who are done wasting time. Every member is screened thoroughly, so the profiles you see are people worth dating.


All of that, the screening, the matches, the marketing, the subscriptions, runs on data. Every AI model and feature that we ship next is built on the data you own.

Goal of the Role

You build and run the systems that move our data; from the product database, app events, attribution and payment providers into Snowflake - the central analytical database that streams data to various destinations. Everything the company decides sits on top of what you build.


You'll be part of our engineering team, reporting to the Head of Engineering. But you set the technical direction for data: architecture, tooling, standards and roadmap come from you, backed by reasoning your manager can follow and trust.


We're building toward being an AI-native company, and data is the constraint on how far that goes. Claude Code is part of how we work day to day. Engineers build with it, and we're moving toward agentic workflows for things like error triage and bug fixing. Every AI use case we take on, whether that's smarter screening, matching, or internal tooling, ends up depending on the data being correct, timely and well-modelled. That's the platform you own.

Tech stack: Snowflake, DBT, Dagster, DataBricks, Python, AWS, BigQuery, MySQL, GitHub, ETL/ELT, Tableau, Claude Code, DataDog

Key Result Areas

1. Own the direction of the data platform

This is yours to shape. You form a view of where the platform needs to go, make the call, and bring the reasoning rather than the question. Tooling and architecture decisions come with the tradeoffs; stated cost, complexity, who maintains it, what happens when it breaks. Your roadmap separates the urgent from the structural, and the structural work actually happens.

2. Build and run reliable pipelines

You own how data moves, end to end. The best pipelines are boring ones: they run, and when they don't, you know before anyone else does. Failures are caught by monitoring, not by someone asking why a dashboard is empty. New sources and markets get integrated properly.

3. Engineer for correctness

Correctness is designed in, not checked afterwards. Tests sit at the right layers and failures are actionable instead of noise. Models are incremental and idempotent, so the same run gives the same result. The messy parts; deduplication, late-arriving data, timezones, attribution windows, are handled deliberately.

4. Set the engineering standard for the data stack

You define how data gets built here, and the standard you set outlasts you. Everything is version-controlled, reviewed and covered by CI. Nothing reaches production by hand. Code is readable enough that someone else can pick it up cold, because at some point someone will. Warehouse spend is watched, and access is managed as code.

5. Be the data counterpart the rest of the company can rely on

Data isn't a reporting function here. Screening, matching, marketing, subscriptions and increasingly our AI tooling all run on what you build, which means most of the company touches your models whether they know it or not. You're close to the business, upstream and downstream, so your work lands visibly and fast.


What Will Help You Be Successful

  • Senior experience owning a production data platform end to end

  • Deep hands-on Snowflake, dbt modelling, and confidence with Dagster or a comparable orchestrator

  • You use AI tooling seriously in your own work and have a view on where it helps and where it doesn't

  • Experience with building APIs using Python

  • Comfortable in AWS, the infrastructure your pipelines run on isn't a black box to you

  • You've integrated third-party sources before: event tracking, attribution, payment and subscription data

  • You handle deduplication, late-arriving data, timezones and attribution windows deliberately, not reactively

  • You form a view, state it, and own the outcome and can explain the tradeoff to a non-data manager

  • You trace problems to root cause, raise issues early, write things down, and follow through


What We Offer

  • A career opportunity that makes a positive impact on people's lives

  • A competitive salary matched with your experience and ambition

  • An amazing work environment in our office at Prins Hendrikkade, at the heart of Amsterdam

  • A MacBook or other hardware of your choice to be able to do your job

  • Stay healthy and bring-your-own-device allowance

  • Training and development budget

  • Frequent team get-togethers and team activities

  • Free Inner Circle VIP membership for you and your single friends


About Inner Circle

Inner Circle is a dating app built on the contrarian belief: opposites don't attract. The best connections happen between people who already live life the same way. So we don't sell more options, or better odds. We sell relevance, people worth dating. Every member is screened, so effort and intention are in place before anyone gets in. And where every other app is built to keep you swiping, ours is built to get you off it, and onto a date with someone worth your time.

At Inner Circle, we embrace our diverse community and team. We celebrate differences and know that they are key for helping us grow. Our team consists of 40 team members, with 16 nationalities and a female: male ratio of 60 : 40. Whatever your race, religion, colour, gender, national origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability or age, we make sure everyone has the space to be themselves.

Mosaic Community Health prides itself on being an innovative health system that pioneers unique and creative ways to provide and improve patient access to health care. Since our founding in 2002 we have proudly served insured and uninsured patients regardless of age, ethnicity, or income.

title: Opportunity for Data Engineer
description:
Data Engineer (8+ Years Experience) – Heavy Data Analytics Project

Tech Stack: Spark, PySpark, Scala, Python, SQL, Databricks, Data Lake, Data Warehouse, Snowflake, Azure (ADF/Synapse/ADLS)

Expected Skill set as per customer– Azure Databricks, Spark, Python, Delta Table, Snowflake basics, and prior experience on data ingestion/transformation.

About the Role

We are hiring a Data Engineer with strong hands-on experience in building high‑performance data pipelines for a heavy data analytics project. The candidate must be excellent at writing complex aggregations, understanding business processes and analytical requirements, and designing scalable data lake and data warehouse solutions. Experience across multiple data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, Azure Data Factory, Synapse, etc.) is a strong advantage.

Key Responsibilities

1. Data Pipeline & ETL/ELT Development

• Develop, optimize, and productionize Spark (PySpark/Scala) pipelines.

• Ingest, transform, cleanse, and aggregate large datasets from varied sources.

• Implement scalable ETL/ELT logic for batch and near-real-time pipelines.

• Apply best practices in partitioning, caching, Delta Lake optimization, and performance tuning.

2. Heavy Data Analytics & Business Understanding

• Write complex aggregation logic (window functions, rollups, grouping sets, analytical functions).

• Understand business KPIs, metrics, and analytical use cases.

• Translate business needs into technical transformations and data models.

• Validate data outputs against business logic and analytics expectations.

• Collaborate with analysts on calculations: weekly/monthly aggregates, trend lines, performance metrics, dimensional rollups.

• Ensure accuracy, consistency, and traceability of business-critical metrics.

3. Data Lake Engineering

• Build and maintain multi-layer Data Lake architectures (Bronze/Silver/Gold).

• Work with Parquet, Delta Lake, ORC, and columnar storage formats.

• Implement schema evolution, auditing, and metadata strategies.

4. Data Warehouse Engineering

• Design dimensional models: Star Schema and Snowflake Schema.

• Build fact and dimension tables supporting analytics and reporting.

• Optimize table structures, keys, and partitioning strategies.

5. Databricks (Added Advantage)

• Develop notebooks/jobs using PySpark/Scala.

• Manage clusters, workflows, and Delta Live Tables.

• Implement best practices for performance and cost efficiency.

6. SQL Engineering

• Strong command of SQL for aggregations, analytical functions, joins, profiling, and validation.

• Write and optimize complex queries supporting dashboards, metrics, and reports.

7. Cloud Data Platforms

Azure: Data Factory, Synapse Analytics, ADLS Gen2, Azure Functions (optional).

Snowflake: Virtual Warehouses, Snowpipe, Streams & Tasks, performance tuning.

8. Data Quality & Documentation

• Validate transformation logic against business rules.

• Document data flows, transformation rules, aggregation logic, and data dictionary/metadata.

• Work with QA and analysts to ensure outputs match business expectations.

Required Qualifications

• 5+ years of hands-on data engineering experience.

• Strong programming skills: Spark, Scala, Python.

• Strong SQL skills (aggregations, analytical functions, large joins).

• Experience with Data Lake and Data Warehouse concepts.

• Experience with Spark-based processing (delta optimization, shuffle tuning, partitioning).

• Experience with at least one cloud data ecosystem (Azure/AWS/GCP).

Preferred Skills

• Experience with Databricks (highly desirable).

• Experience with Snowflake or modern cloud DWH.

• Experience with ADF/Synapse/Airflow/dbt for orchestration.

• Knowledge of CI/CD for data pipelines.

• Experience with large-scale data analytics environments.

Soft Skills

• Strong understanding of business logic behind analytics outputs.

• Ability to translate business metrics into technical transformations.

• Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.

• Good communication and cross-team collaboration.

Pay: $85,000 - $94,000 annually, depending on experience


The Pacific Island Region (PIR) of NOAA’s Office of National Marine Sanctuaries manages the Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale National Marine Sanctuary, Papahanaumokuakea National Marine Sanctuary, and the National Marine Sanctuary of American Samoa. The PIR staff are located across multiple islands. The work is accomplished with personnel with varying responsibilities, including sanctuary management, education, outreach, research, resource protection, facility operations, and administration.

We are looking for an Environmental Planner (Marine Protected Area Planning & Evaluation) to provide various planning and evaluation support tasks for the team, working primarily in Honolulu, Hawaii, at NOAA’s Inouye Regional Center.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • Support the continued development of the site evaluation strategy and other site management plans;
  • Implement and test existing evaluation strategy methods;
  • Coordinate with partner agencies in the collection and analysis of identified metrics for evaluation;
  • Coordinate with partners and Sanctuary staff to incorporate program information in the Sanctuary Management Plan tracking tool;
  • Support the development and production of the annual review of Sanctuary Management Plan implementation;
  • Support the preparation of a five-year Sanctuary Status Report based on information in annual reports, monitoring results, and evaluation efforts;
  • Support meetings with partner agencies to identify changes and updates needed to the Sanctuary Management Plan;
  • Support managers with the development of management plans and the management plan review process, including writing environmental impact statements, reviewing and drafting responses to public comments, staffing public meetings, developing focal area plans for key action areas (such as outreach, education, interpretation, and
  • research plans), and developing site resource requirements;
  • Support the development of PIR site step-down plans called for in the Management Plan;
  • Support site leadership and the Sanctuary Advisory Council (SAC) to plan and carry out quarterly SAC meetings;
  • Support site leadership in policy development and implementation and assess potential impacts; and
  • Support the region and sites in coordinating the review and clearance of necessary processes with headquarters and other partners.

The role gathers and documents specifications, coordinates larger IT projects (including those involving client requirements), and works closely with business leadership to help prioritise IT's workload against broader business objectives.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Business Liaison & Requirements Gathering

  • Liaise with IT and other business departments to identify and understand IT system and application improvement needs.
  • Act as the first point of contact for business units raising system, process, or application improvement ideas.
  • Translate business problems and opportunities into clear functional and technical requirements for IT to action.

Specifications & Documentation

  • Facilitate the development of specifications with business stakeholders, ensuring requirements are complete, accurate, and agreed.
  • Follow up with business units to obtain outstanding information needed to progress specifications or projects.
  • Maintain clear documentation of requirements, decisions, and changes throughout each initiative.

Project Management

  • Capture and manage client requirements where projects involve external client input or deliverables.
  • Coordinate with technical teams, vendors, and business stakeholders to keep projects on track.

Prioritisation & Business Alignment

  • Work with leadership across the business to prioritise the IT work program in line with business priorities and resourcing.
  • Provide regular updates to leadership and stakeholders on project status, risks, and outcomes.

  • Intermediate data analysis skills (e.g., Excel, SQL, Power BI) to support requirements validation and reporting.
  • General understanding of system integrations, APIs, and data flows between business applications.
  • Awareness of IT security, privacy, and compliance considerations relevant to system and process changes.

Role Requirements

  • Experience in a business analyst, systems analyst, or IT liaison capacity.
  • Tertiary qualification in information systems, business, IT, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience).
  • Demonstrated experience managing IT projects of varying scale, including those with external client requirements.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce clear specifications and status reporting.

title: Staff RF Engineer

At CesiumAstro, we are developers and pioneers of out-of-the-box communication systems for satellites, UAVs, launch vehicles, and other space and airborne platforms. We take pride in our dynamic and cross-functional work environment, which allows us to learn, develop, and engage across our organization. We are actively seeking passionate, collaborative, energetic, and forward-thinking individuals to join our team.
The Skylark product line is focused on the rapid design, build, and test of cutting-edge active phased array antennas (AESA) for terrestrial and airborne applications. Current programs span high-power, large-scale ground terminals for missile defense to commercial airline and helicopter connectivity solutions.

We are actively seeking passionate, collaborative, energetic, and forward-thinking individual to join our team as a Staff RF Engineer. The ideal candidate has extensive experience in board-level and system-level RF electronics design. If you enjoy working in a startup environment and are passionate about developing leading-edge phased arrays for satellites, spacecraft, and aerospace systems, we would like to hear from you.
In this position, you will be responsible for RF circuits, modules, and systems through all phases of the development process. The ideal candidate will be proficient in board-level schematic design and PCB layout of RF circuits, system-level communications concepts such as link budgets and modulation schemes, and end-to-end RF product development. The work will include many aspects of phased array communication systems, including RF front ends, frequency converters and synthesizers, filters, beamformers, power dividers, and phased array antennas.
As a staff hardware team member, you will be responsible for RF system and hardware designs from initial concept through requirements definition, architecture definition, part selection, detailed design, analysis, manufacturing, testing, qualification, and in-orbit support of Cesium's products. Hardware design tasks will include block diagrams, detailed schematics, PCB layout and routing, simulations, and test design.   • Bachelor of Science (BS)) degree in Electrical Engineering (EE) from an accredited university or institution. Master of Science (MS) desired.
  • Minimum of 8 years of industry experience in design and analysis of RF electronics and systems.
  • Expert-level proficiency in professional simulation tools such as CST and ADS, as well as EDA tools such Altium.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with lab instruments such as vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred experience includes:

  • Python or other programming languages.
  • Aerospace electronics design, development, and qualification.
  • Worst-case circuit analysis, failure method and criticality analyses, and reliability analysis.
  • Antenna design
  • EMI/EMC design and mitigation techniques.

title: AI Security Researcher
description:
DESE Research, Inc. is seeking a talented, motivated, and enthusiastic AI Security and Safety Assurance Researcher to join a multidisciplinary team of analysts, researchers, developers, and engineers. This role focuses on constructing and evaluating risk analysis and assurance methodologies as they apply to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) within mission-critical defense systems. If you are passionate about responsible AI, risk analysis, and enhancing the resilience of military systems, we want to hear from you!

Job Details:

The candidate will work as part of a small team in conducting research, developing and executing assurance methodologies, and identifying areas of risk, threats, and vulnerabilities associated with AI systems, pipelines, and components. To be successful in this role, the candidate will need knowledge and understanding of Army acquisition, emerging DoW and Army guidance; AI/ML security and safety; and assurance methodologies. A successful candidate will possess strong analytical skills, communicate effectively with technical teams and customers, and thrive in a collaborative engineering environment. This role is on-site in Huntsville, AL.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct research and analysis on Responsible/Ethical AI concepts, initiatives, and evaluation methods.
  • Identify AI-enabled system functionality and critical components by analyzing and decomposing complex systems from documentation as well as input from engineering subject matter experts.
  • Develop and apply risk analysis and assessment methodologies for AI/ML in mission-critical systems.
  • Collaborate with Acquisition, AI/ML, Software Engineering, and Systems Engineering teams to ensure survivability and resiliency of warfighting systems.
  • Produce high-quality technical writing and oral presentations on research findings, incorporating data from disparate sources or organizations into a cohesive narrative.
  • Build meaningful relationships with researchers and stakeholders across organizations.
  • Stay informed on advancements in AI risk analysis, governance, and DoW initiatives.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, Software Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5 years of experience in security assurance, risk management, AI/ML governance, or related field.
  • Active Secret security clearance or the ability to obtain and maintain one.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated excellence in independent research across academia, industry, or government.
  • Proficiency in technical writing and effectively communicating research results.
  • Strong critical thinking and analytic skills.
  • Self-motivated, proactive, and adaptable to changing project needs.
  • Ability to foster collaboration within a multidisciplinary team while supporting a customer-facing engineering environment.
  • Understanding of AI development lifecycle processes and MLSecOps best practices.
  • Experience in AI threat modeling, AI risk research, or related disciplines.
  • Experience training and using Machine Learning models.
  • Experience using AI observability, tracing, and evaluation tools (e.g., MLflow, Langfuse).
  • Experience with adversarial testing methods and AI red-teaming tools.
  • Familiarity with ML frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) and AI orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex).
  • Experience with the DoW AI Assurance Toolkit or other AI policy and guidance initiatives.
  • Awareness of evolving AI regulations, standards, and best practices.
  • Familiarity with Army acquisition lifecycles and System Security Engineering.
  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks, standards, and controls (e.g., NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF), ISO/IEC 42001, NIST COSAiS Project).
  • Familiarity with ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems) or similar frameworks.
  • Knowledge of weapon systems, embedded system platforms, and AI-enabled defense systems.

DESE is committed to creating a company that is known for its respect and care for employees. We understand that happy employees are what keeps our business going and we strive to provide the best opportunities for each individual working on our team! Here are a few reasons you will love working for DESE:

· Competitive salaries

· Annual performance bonuses

· Robust 401K profit sharing plan

· Competitive health, dental & vision insurance with affordable premiums

· Two different flexible spending account options

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Senior Data Engineer — Azure Data Platform & Master Data | Metz


Location: Metz, France Working Hours: German-aligned (CET business hours) Function: Data Engineering Seniority: Senior (5+ years)


About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Data Engineer to build and own our Azure-based data platform — the pipelines, the warehouse, and above all, the master data quality layer that turns messy, multi-system data into trusted, deduplicated golden records.

This is an upstream engineering role. If you care more about data quality and integration than dashboards, this is built for you.


MBB Background Only: Candidates must come from the data & analytics practice of a top-tier strategy consultancy — McKinsey / QuantumBlack, BCG / BCG X, or Bain / Bain Advanced Analytics — or an equivalent premium data consultancy. We're looking for people who've built real data platforms under high client-delivery standards, not just advised on them.


What You'll Do
  • Design and build robust ETL/ELT pipelines on Azure (Azure SQL, Data Factory / Fabric pipelines, Python).
  • Own Master Data Management as a first-class discipline: data cleansing, deduplication, entity resolution, fuzzy matching, golden record creation, and survivorship rules — starting with our customer and product masters.
  • Integrate data across core enterprise systems: ERP, CRM, PIM, warehouse management, and eCommerce platforms.
  • Design and maintain dimensional data models and modern data warehouse architecture.
  • Build data governance foundations: validation frameworks, quality monitoring, lineage, and documentation.


What You Bring
  • 5+ years in Data Engineering or Analytics Engineering with real pipeline ownership (not just contributing to someone else's).
  • Advanced SQL and strong Python for data workflows.
  • Azure data platform experience (Azure SQL, ADF/Fabric) — or equivalent cloud depth with a credible ability to ramp onto Azure fast.
  • Hands-on master data experience — you can walk through, step by step, how you deduplicated and consolidated a real messy dataset.
  • Experience integrating ERP/CRM/operational systems — any major ERP ecosystem counts (Dynamics/Business Central, SAP, Odoo, NetSuite, or similar). What matters is that you've worked with ERP data models before.
  • Able to work German-aligned business hours (CET) for close collaboration with the core team.


MBB Background Only — McKinsey (QuantumBlack), BCG (BCG X), or Bain (Bain Advanced Analytics), or equivalent top-tier consultancy.


Nice to have: working knowledge of Power BI — this is not a reporting role, so it's a bonus, not a requirement.


Why This Role

You won't be maintaining someone else's pipeline — you'll be the person who decides what "trusted data" means for the business and builds the system that delivers it. High ownership, high visibility, direct impact on every downstream system that touches customer and product data.

title: Principal Safety Case Engineer
description:
About us

Founded in 2017, Wayve is the leading developer of Embodied AI technology. Our advanced AI software and foundation models enable vehicles to perceive, understand, and navigate any complex environment, enhancing the usability and safety of automated driving systems.

Our vision is to create autonomy that propels the world forward. Our intelligent, mapless, and hardware-agnostic AI products are designed for automakers, accelerating the transition from assisted to automated driving.

In our fast-paced environment big problems ignite us—we embrace uncertainty, leaning into complex challenges to unlock groundbreaking solutions. We aim high and stay humble in our pursuit of excellence, constantly learning and evolving as we pave the way for a smarter, safer future.

At Wayve, your contributions matter. We value diversity, embrace new perspectives, and foster an inclusive work environment; we back each other to deliver impact.

Make Wayve the experience that defines your career!

The role

We are looking for a Principal Safety Case Engineer to own the architecture, strategy and integrity of Wayve’s safety cases for our first products. This role sits independently from Engineering and Product and reports into Safety Management & Assurance, providing senior expert safety oversight while working closely with the teams responsible for designing, developing, validating and releasing the product.

You will act as the architect of the safety case: defining the top-level claims, argumentation structure, evidence strategy and assurance approach that connect product intent, system behavior, AI performance, engineering controls, validation and operational deployment into a coherent safety argument. You will provide independent challenge and advice, while enabling Engineering and Product teams to own and deliver the safety evidence required for their systems.

What You’ll Be Doing

Safety Case Strategy & Architecture

  • Own the safety case strategy and architecture for Wayve’s robotaxi and OEM ADAS products.
  • Define top-level safety claims, argumentation, evidence structures, and traceability from safety requirements through validation and deployment decisions.
  • Develop safety arguments appropriate for AI-enabled autonomous driving, incorporating functional safety, SOTIF, AI safety, cybersecurity, validation, operational safety, and post-deployment monitoring.
  • Evolve reusable safety case approaches as Wayve’s products, vehicle platforms, and evidence base mature.

Product & Engineering Integration

  • Partner with Product, Systems Engineering, AI/ML, Validation, Vehicle Engineering, Software, Hardware, and Operational Safety to define safety requirements and evidence expectations.
  • Identify gaps, assumptions, and weaknesses in the safety argument early and drive resolution with accountable teams.
  • Ensure product requirements, architecture, validation plans, and release criteria remain aligned with the safety case.
  • Support technical and program leaders in making proportionate, evidence-based safety decisions.

Independent Safety Assurance

  • Provide independent technical challenge of safety cases and supporting evidence.
  • Assess whether safety arguments are coherent, complete, evidence-backed, and sufficient to support release or deployment.
  • Highlight material gaps, uncertainties, dependencies, residual risks, and safety red lines.
  • Provide clear recommendations to safety governance forums and senior leadership.

Safety Leadership

  • Build a common understanding of safety case principles across Wayve.
  • Coach engineering and product leaders on structured safety argumentation, evidence quality, and traceability.
  • Represent the safety case perspective in internal governance, customer, and technical discussions.
  • Contribute to Wayve’s broader safety strategy and assurance capability.

About You

Essential Experience

  • Deep experience developing or owning safety cases for complex safety-critical systems, ideally in autonomous vehicles, ADAS, robotics, aerospace, defense, or another software-intensive domain.
  • Strong systems engineering background spanning requirements, architecture, verification, validation, and safety assurance.
  • Proven ability to translate complex technical evidence into structured safety claims and arguments.
  • Strong understanding of autonomous driving and AI/ML safety, including model performance, data, uncertainty, and limitations of conventional verification approaches.
  • Experience partnering with AI/ML, engineering, systems, and product teams on safety-critical products.
  • Strong knowledge of relevant standards, including ISO 26262, ISO 21448, ISO/PAS 8800, and ISO 3450x.
  • Excellent technical communication and stakeholder management skills.

Desirable

  • Safety case experience with L2+/L3 ADAS or L4 ADS products.
  • Experience with GSN or equivalent structured assurance methods.
  • Safety evidence experience for end-to-end or foundation-model-based autonomous driving.
  • Experience working with OEMs, regulators, assessors, or independent safety reviewers.
  • Familiarity with operational and post-deployment safety monitoring.

What we’re looking for

  • You are an architect and systems thinker who can move comfortably between top-level safety strategy and detailed technical evidence.
  • You are pragmatic and able to distinguish between what is essential to the safety argument and what is merely desirable.
  • You are intellectually rigorous, curious and comfortable challenging assumptions, including established industry practice where it does not adequately address AI-enabled autonomous driving.
  • You can work independently of Engineering and Product without becoming detached from them: your role is to provide credible challenge, direction and oversight while helping teams succeed.
  • You are comfortable operating with uncertainty and can make clear recommendations based on the strength of the available evidence.
  • You are open to challenge and willing to change your position when better evidence emerges.
  • You can clearly articulate where you believe a safety red line exists, why it matters, and what evidence or mitigation would be required to move it.

Success in this role

  • A clear and credible safety case architecture exists for Wayve’s first robotaxi and OEM ADAS products.
  • Engineering and Product teams understand the safety claims they support and the evidence they are responsible for delivering.
  • Safety gaps and weak assumptions are identified early enough to influence product decisions rather than being discovered at the end of a program.
  • Wayve develops a safety argument for AI-enabled autonomous driving that is technically rigorous, scalable and capable of standing up to scrutiny from customers, regulators and independent assessors.
  • Senior safety and product governance has an independent, evidence-based view of whether the safety case is sufficiently strong to support release and deployment decisions.


This role is a full-time role based in Sunnyvale, CA (hybrid) and the reasonably estimated salary for this role ranges from $290,000 to 426,300, plus a competitive equity package. Actual compensation is based on the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. At Wayve we want the best of all worlds so we operate a hybrid working policy that combines time together in our offices and workshops to fuel innovation, culture, relationships and learning, and time spent working from home. We understand that everyone has a unique set of skills and experiences and that not everyone will meet all of the requirements listed above. If you’re passionate about self-driving cars and think you have what it takes to make a positive impact on the world, we encourage you to apply.

title: Data Ingestion Engineer
description:
The Role

As a Data Ingestion Engineer, you will design and build the systems that pull health data from a diverse and growing set of sources — wearables (Apple Health, Fitbit, Oura, Whoop, etc.), connected medical devices (glucose monitors, BP cuffs, ECG patches), lab and diagnostic feeds, EHR / HL7-FHIR systems, and patient-reported data — and land it reliably into Nickel's platform in a form doctors and downstream systems can trust.

You will work at the intersection of high-volume streaming data, healthcare interoperability standards, and strict data integrity requirements — building pipelines where "mostly correct" is not good enough, because a doctor may be making a call based on your data.


What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and operate ingestion pipelines for structured and unstructured health data from multiple device APIs, third-party health platforms, and clinical data sources
  • Build integrations with wearable/device SDKs and health data standards (Apple HealthKit, Google Health Connect, HL7/FHIR, DICOM where relevant)
  • Architect for reliability at the edges — handling intermittent connectivity, device data gaps, duplicate/out-of-order events, and vendor API instability gracefully
  • Implement data validation, normalization, and schema management so heterogeneous sources land in a consistent, queryable format
  • Build real-time and batch ingestion paths depending on data criticality (e.g., an arrhythmia alert vs. a weekly step count)
  • Work closely with platform, ML, and clinical product teams to understand what "usable" data looks like for diagnostic and care-decision use cases
  • Own data quality, lineage, and observability for your pipelines — you'll know when something's wrong before a doctor does
  • Implement ingestion in a way that's compliant with healthcare data privacy requirements (HIPAA and equivalent Indian data protection standards)


What We're Looking For

  • 3–7 years of experience building data pipelines, ideally with high-volume, real-time, or IoT/device data
  • Strong programming skills in Python, Go, or Java, with production experience in distributed data systems
  • Hands-on experience with streaming/event infrastructure (Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, or similar)
  • Experience with API integrations at scale — OAuth flows, rate limiting, retry/backoff strategies, webhook handling
  • Solid understanding of data modeling and schema design for messy, multi-source data
  • Exposure to healthcare data standards (HL7, FHIR, DICOM) is a strong plus — not mandatory, but a fast-track signal
  • Experience with cloud-native data infra (AWS/GCP, tools like Airflow, dbt, Spark, or similar)
  • A bias toward reliability and correctness over cleverness — this is data that informs medical decisions
  • Comfort working in a 0-to-1 environment: this team is being built now, so you're shaping the architecture, not inheriting it


Why This Role

  • You're not integrating "some device" — you're building the layer that makes continuous, diagnostics-led care technically possible
  • Ground-floor architectural ownership: the ingestion patterns you set now become the platform's data spine
  • Backed by an eight-figure raise and a founding team with a track record — startup pace, with real capital behind it
  • India isn't a delivery arm here — this is the core build team for Nickel's platform

title: Vice President of Laboratory Services
description:
Title: Vice President of Laboratory Services

Location: Remote (Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Idaho, Maryland, Montana, New Mexico, North Carolina, North Dakota, Oregon, Texas, Washington) + Travel to Renton, WA

Salary: $180,000


PURPOSE OF POSITION: The Vice President of Laboratory Services provides strategic, operational, clinical, and regulatory leadership for the organization's centralized laboratory serving a nationwide network of outpatient substance use disorder treatment clinics. This executive leader is responsible for ensuring that the laboratory delivers high-quality, compliant, timely, and cost-effective diagnostic testing that supports patient care, regulatory compliance, and organizational growth.

The Vice President oversees all aspects of laboratory operations, including strategic planning, regulatory compliance, quality management, financial performance, laboratory technology, workforce development, client service, and business continuity. This position serves as the executive responsible for laboratory accreditation, operational excellence, innovation, and long-term strategic planning.


JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The following functions have been determined by Ideal Option to be essential to the successful performance of this position which includes but is not limited to:


Executive Leadership

• Develop and execute the strategic vision for laboratory services aligned with organizational goals.

• Serve as the executive leader responsible for laboratory performance nationwide.

• Participate as a member of executive leadership committees.

• Develop annual strategic initiatives, capital plans, and operational goals.

• Lead organizational planning related to laboratory growth, expansion, automation, and technology.

• Provide executive reporting on laboratory performance, quality metrics, regulatory compliance, financial results, and operational risks.

• Build collaborative relationships across all departments supporting enterprise initiatives.

• Promote a culture centered on patient safety, quality, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.


Laboratory Operations

Provide executive oversight and strategic leadership for all laboratory operations, including toxicology and clinical testing, specimen accessioning, processing, chain of custody, confirmation testing, result reporting, and laboratory customer service. Oversee courier and logistics operations, inventory and supply chain management, equipment maintenance, and vendor relationships to ensure efficient and reliable laboratory services.


Ensure laboratory operations consistently meet performance expectations related to turnaround times, specimen integrity, testing accuracy, productivity, capacity management, service level agreements, and client satisfaction. Develop and implement scalable operational models, processes, and resources that support continued organizational growth while maintaining quality, efficiency, compliance, and service excellence.


Regulatory Compliance

Maintain organizational compliance with all applicable federal, state, and industry regulations and standards, including CLIA, The Joint Commission, COLA (if applicable), state laboratory licensing requirements, DEA, OSHA, HIPAA, CMS, and FDA requirements where applicable. Lead and ensure successful completion of federal and state inspections, accreditation surveys, internal audits, and external audits. Develop proactive compliance monitoring systems to identify regulatory risks, address deficiencies, and implement timely corrective actions to maintain ongoing compliance and operational readiness.


Quality Management

Represent laboratory in enterprise-wide quality improvement initiatives.Provide executive oversight and leadership for laboratory quality management, including continuous quality improvement, quality assurance and control, proficiency testing, root cause investigations, incident reporting, document control, validation programs, and competency assessments. Monitor key laboratory quality indicators, including error rates, specimen rejection, turnaround times, provider leadership concerns, corrective actions, and patient safety events. Lead efforts to identify and resolve quality issues while promoting continuous improvement, operational excellence, and patient safety. Represent laboratory operations in enterprise-wide quality improvement initiatives.


Financial Leadership

Develop, manage, and provide strategic oversight of laboratory operating and capital budgets, including financial forecasting, cost management, productivity analysis, supply expense management, vendor negotiations, capital equipment planning, and contract management. Monitor key financial metrics, including cost per test, cost per accession, labor productivity, and equipment utilization. Identify and implement opportunities to improve operational efficiency and reduce costs while maintaining laboratory quality, service, and patient safety.


Laboratory Technology

Provide strategic leadership and oversight of laboratory technology, including the Laboratory Information System (LIS), laboratory automation, instrumentation, interface management, electronic ordering and reporting, middleware, and data analytics. Partner with Information Technology to ensure laboratory systems remain secure, reliable, integrated, and scalable. Lead the evaluation, selection, and implementation of emerging technologies that enhance laboratory operations, quality, efficiency, and organizational growth.


Clinical Partnership

Collaborate with the Medical Director, providers, and clinical operations leadership to ensure laboratory services effectively support medication-assisted treatment (MAT), urine drug testing, confirmation testing, clinical decision-making, patient safety, and evidence-based treatment. Provide laboratory expertise and guidance in the development and implementation of clinical protocols and practices.


Growth and Business Development

Support organizational expansion and business development initiatives by assessing laboratory capacity, developing scalable workflows, planning staffing models, evaluating new testing capabilities, and supporting new clinic openings, mergers and acquisitions, and due diligence for laboratory integration opportunities. Evaluate opportunities to expand testing services and establish strategic partnerships that support organizational growth and laboratory capabilities.


People Leadership

Provide strategic leadership and oversight for laboratory management, including the Laboratory Director, three Laboratory Managers, and Procurement Specialist. Lead organizational design, workforce and succession planning, leadership development, employee engagement, performance management, recruitment, retention, coaching, and mentoring. Foster an inclusive, collaborative, and high-performance culture focused on accountability, professional development, operational excellence, and employee success.


Risk Management

Identify, assess, and mitigate operational risks related to testing quality, regulatory compliance, business continuity, staffing, information security, disaster recovery, equipment failures, supply shortages, and patient safety. Develop, maintain, and implement laboratory emergency preparedness and business continuity plans to support operational resilience and uninterrupted services.


Vendor Management

Provide strategic oversight of laboratory vendor relationships, including instrument manufacturers, reference laboratories, supply vendors, technology partners, courier services, and maintenance providers. Negotiate and manage contracts, establish performance expectations, and monitor vendor performance to ensure quality, reliability, cost-effectiveness, and alignment with laboratory and organizational needs.


Performance Metrics

Develop and maintain executive dashboards and performance reporting for key laboratory metrics, including turnaround time, test volumes, productivity, financial performance, quality indicators, regulatory findings, customer satisfaction, staffing metrics, equipment utilization, and growth metrics. Analyze performance trends, identify opportunities for improvement, and present laboratory performance reports to executive leadership and Board committees, as appropriate.


Additional Responsibilities

Maintain compliance with national Protected Health Information (PHI) requirements, including HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2, and protect the confidentiality of sensitive organizational information. Maintain consistent and reliable attendance, work cooperatively with others as part of the Ideal Option team, and perform other projects and duties as assigned.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

Must be reliable, highly trustworthy, organized, and detail-oriented, with the ability to maintain confidential and meticulous records. Proficiency with Microsoft Office products, including Outlook, Teams, and Excel, is required.


Demonstrated expertise in clinical laboratory operations, toxicology testing, laboratory regulations and CLIA requirements, CAP or The Joint Commission accreditation, quality management systems, financial management, strategic planning, executive leadership, change management, Lean process improvement, Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), data analytics, operational excellence, healthcare compliance, risk management, vendor negotiations, talent development, healthcare reimbursement, and project management.


Strong ability to influence executive leaders, build and maintain cross-functional partnerships, lead organizational change, analyze complex operational and financial data, develop and execute long-term strategies, communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences, solve complex operational challenges, and make informed, data-driven decisions.
